title: Audit pairs reveal the file drawer by comparing hidden denominators with published numerators
summary: This pattern candidate says the missing denominator becomes visible through paired surfaces: FDA packages versus journals, protocols versus articles, registries/inception cohorts versus publications, and review methods that search hard-to-access evidence. The pattern is deliberately framed as a source-acquisition method, not a universal prevalence estimate.

status_history.note: Seed emphasized negative results/file drawer and asked for structural causes rather than lists.
Promoted using five meta-research audit records and six source records.

place.scope: biomedical/clinical-research evidence system first pass; pattern may generalize only after cross-field records

claims.claim: Rev0009 meta-research records support an audit-pair pattern: file-drawer and selective-reporting bias become empirically visible when an inception, protocol, registry, or regulator denominator is compared with the published literature numerator.
what_would_change_status: A future taxonomy finds these audit designs too heterogeneous for one pattern family.

claims.claim: The pattern requires separating study-level disappearance from outcome-level disappearance: an unpublished trial, a delayed publication, a published trial with omitted outcomes, and a publication whose framing conflicts with regulator/protocol conclusions are different record states.
what_would_change_status: A later lifecycle schema makes this pattern claim redundant or more precise.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0009 is not a universal prevalence estimate, not a claim that all positive findings are biased, and not a misconduct inference; it is a source-acquisition rule for how to reveal the missing denominator.
what_would_change_status: A mature cross-domain quantitative synthesis justifies stronger prevalence claims or splits the pattern by field/time/infrastructure.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass extraction from peer-reviewed/open/institutional article pages and indexed abstracts
limitations: Medical/clinical research is overrepresented in rev0009.
The pattern is about evidence acquisition and record state, not final prevalence.

evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0016 scaffold added; controls not yet promoted

shared_structure: identify a denominator surface that exists before or outside publication
compare it with the published/discoverable literature surface
classify missing, delayed, reframed, or incompletely reported evidence without inferring motive
subtypes: systematic review of empirical reporting-bias cohorts
method review of dissemination bias and hard-to-access evidence
failure_modes: matching denominator records to publications fails
published article exists but outcomes/framing changed
statistical diagnostics substitute for source acquisition
negative_controls_needed: Registered Reports with null findings published as planned
FDA/regulator cohorts with no selective publication signal
audits where suspected unpublished studies are found to be published under unlinked identifiers

positive_controls_needed: Add additional paired-audit studies comparing a hidden denominator surface with a published numerator surface.
negative_controls_needed: Add paired audits showing little or no publication/reporting bias in a specific domain or period.
counterexamples_to_seek: A denominator surface later shown incomplete enough that the audit pair itself must be downgraded.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: Medium: study non-publication, outcome switching, effect-size inflation, and dissemination lag should not be collapsed.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.

handling_notes: Use reporting-bias audits to improve evidence systems, not to shame authors or sponsors by default.
Publication and outcome gaps may arise from incentives, policies, resource constraints, editorial decisions, study failures, or misconduct; state only what the source supports.
Clinical-treatment implications require domain experts and current guidelines; the cube is epistemic infrastructure, not medical advice.
